sanskrit: anyeṣām api naśyanti suhṛdaś ca dhanāni ca paśya buddhyā manuṣyāṇāṃ rājann āpadam ātmanaḥ niyaccha yaccha saṃyaccha indriyāṇi mano giram
english: For others too friends and riches alike are lost; behold with your understanding, O king, the calamities that befall men, and your own. Restrain, hold back, control utterly your senses, your mind, and your speech.

sanskrit: pratiṣiddhān avāpyeṣu durlabheṣv ahiteṣu ca pratikṛṣṭeṣu bhāveṣu vyatikṛṣṭeṣv asaṃbhave prajñānatṛpto vikrāntas tvadvidho nānuśocati
english: Over things forbidden and unattainable, hard to win or harmful, over conditions that are debased or perverse, over what cannot come to be — a man like you, content in wisdom and bold of spirit, does not grieve.

sanskrit: alpam icchann acapalo mṛdur dāntaḥ susaṃśitaḥ brahmacaryopapannaś ca tvadvidho naiva muhyati
english: Desiring little, steady, gentle, self-controlled, well-disciplined, and endowed with continence, a man like you is never bewildered.

sanskrit: na tv eva jālmīṃ kāpālīṃ vṛttim eṣitum arhasi nṛśaṃsavṛttiṃ pāpiṣṭhāṃ duḥkhāṃ kāpuruṣocitām
english: But you should never seek the vile, skull-bearer's way of life — a cruel calling, most sinful, full of misery, befitting only a base man.

sanskrit: api mūlaphalājīvo ramasvaiko mahāvane vāgyataḥ saṃgṛhītātmā sarvabhūtadayānvitaḥ
english: Better to live on roots and fruits and delight alone in the great forest, guarded in speech, self-possessed, filled with compassion for all beings.

sanskrit: sadṛśaṃ paṇḍitasyaitad īṣādantena dantinā yad eko ramate 'raṇye yac cāpy alpena tuṣyati
english: This befits the wise man — like a tusker whose tusks reach to the plough-pole — that he delights alone in the wilderness and is content with little.

sanskrit: mahāhradaḥ saṃkṣubhita ātmanaiva prasīdati etad evaṃgatasyāhaṃ sukhaṃ paśyāmi kevalam
english: A great lake, once stirred, grows clear again of its own accord; for a man who has come to such a state, this alone do I see as true happiness.

sanskrit: asaṃbhave śriyo rājan hīnasya sacivādibhiḥ daive pratiniviṣṭe ca kiṃ śreyo manyate bhavān
english: When prosperity is impossible, O king, for one bereft of ministers and the rest, and when fate is set against him — what does your honour deem to be the greater good?

sanskrit: munir uvāca atha cet pauruṣaṃ kiṃ cit kṣatriyātmani paśyasi bravīmi hanta te nītiṃ rājyasya pratipattaye
english: The sage said: But if you see in yourself, as a warrior, any manly resolve, then come — I will tell you the policy for regaining your kingdom.

sanskrit: tāṃ cec chakṣyasy anuṣṭhātuṃ karma caiva kariṣyasi śṛṇu sarvam aśeṣeṇa yat tvāṃ vakṣyāmi tattvataḥ
english: If you can carry it out, and will perform the deed, then hear in full, without omission, all that I shall tell you truly.

sanskrit: ācariṣyasi cet karma mahato 'rthān avāpsyasi rājyaṃ rājyasya mantraṃ vā mahatīṃ vā punaḥ śriyam yady etad rocate rājan punar brūhi bravīmi te
english: If you will perform the deed, you shall win great rewards — a kingdom, or counsel over a kingdom, or again great prosperity. If this pleases you, O king, say so once more, and I will speak to you.

sanskrit: rājaputra uvāca bravītu bhagavān nītim upapanno 'smy ahaṃ prabho amogham idam adyāstu tvayā saha samāgatam
english: The prince said: Let the blessed one declare the policy; I am ready, O lord. Let this meeting with you today not be in vain.

sanskrit: munir uvāca hitvā stambhaṃ ca mānaṃ ca krodhaharṣau bhayaṃ tathā praty amitraṃ niṣevasva praṇipatya kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: The sage said: Casting off stiffness and pride, anger, elation, and fear alike, attend upon your enemy, bowing low with hands joined.

sanskrit: tam uttamena śaucena karmaṇā cābhirādhaya dātum arhati te vṛttiṃ vaidehaḥ satyasaṃgaraḥ
english: Win him over with the utmost integrity and service; the king of Videha, true to his word, will be ready to grant you a livelihood.

sanskrit: pramāṇaṃ sarvabhūteṣu pragrahaṃ ca gamiṣyasi tataḥ sahāyān sotsāhāṃl lapsyase 'vyasanāñ śucīn
english: You will become an authority among all beings, and a man held in trust; then you will gain helpers — zealous, free of vice, and pure.

sanskrit: vartamānaḥ svaśāstre vai saṃyatātmā jitendriyaḥ abhyuddharati cātmānaṃ prasādayati ca prajāḥ
english: Conducting himself by his own discipline, self-restrained and master of his senses, a man lifts himself up and wins the goodwill of the people.

sanskrit: tenaiva tvaṃ dhṛtimatā śrīmatā cābhisatkṛtaḥ pramāṇaṃ sarvabhūteṣu gatvā pragrahaṇaṃ mahat
english: Honoured by that resolute and prosperous king, you will become an authority among all beings, attaining great trust.

sanskrit: tataḥ suhṛdbalaṃ labdhvā mantrayitvā sumantritam antarair bhedayitvārīn bilvaṃ bilvena śātaya parair vā saṃvidaṃ kṛtvā balam apy asya ghātaya
english: Then, having gathered a force of allies and taken well-considered counsel, divide your foes through their dissensions — split the bilva-fruit with a bilva — or, making compact with rivals, destroy his army as well.

sanskrit: alabhyā ye śubhā bhāvāḥ striyaś cācchādanāni ca śayyāsanāni yānāni mahārhāṇi gṛhāṇi ca
english: Those goodly things that are hard to come by — women and fine garments, couches and seats, chariots, costly mansions —

sanskrit: pakṣiṇo mṛgajātāni rasā gandhāḥ phalāni ca teṣv eva sajjayethās tvaṃ yathā naśyet svayaṃ paraḥ
english: birds, all manner of game, savours, perfumes, and fruits — in these you should ensnare him, so that the foe may ruin himself by his own hand.

sanskrit: yady eva pratiṣeddhavyo yady upekṣaṇam arhati na jātu vivṛtaḥ kāryaḥ śatrur vinayam icchatā
english: Whether he is to be resisted or merely to be ignored, one who seeks his own advancement should never let his enmity stand openly revealed.

sanskrit: vasasva paramāmitraviṣaye prājñasaṃmate bhajasva śvetakākīyair mitrādhamam anarthakaiḥ
english: Dwell in the realm of your bitterest foe, esteemed there as wise; and with white-crow flatteries, worthless though they be, court that meanest of friends.

sanskrit: ārambhāṃś cāsya mahato duṣkarāṃs tvaṃ prayojaya nadībandhavirodhāṃś ca balavadbhir virudhyatām
english: Set him to grand and difficult undertakings — damming rivers and the like — and contrive that he fall into conflict with the powerful.

sanskrit: udyānāni mahārhāṇi śayanāny āsanāni ca pratibhogasukhenaiva kośam asya virecaya
english: With costly pleasure-gardens, beds, and seats — by the very enjoyment of luxuries — drain his treasury empty.

sanskrit: yajñadānapraśaṃsāsmai brāhmaṇeṣv anuvarṇyatām te tvatpriyaṃ kariṣyanti taṃ ceṣyanti vṛkā iva
english: Let praise of sacrifice and of giving be sung to him among the brāhmaṇas; they will do what pleases you, and will prey upon him like wolves.

sanskrit: asaṃśayaṃ puṇyaśīlaḥ prāpnoti paramāṃ gatim triviṣṭape puṇyatamaṃ sthānaṃ prāpnoti pārthivaḥ kośakṣaye tv amitrāṇāṃ vaśaṃ kausalya gacchati
english: No doubt a king of pious character attains the supreme goal and gains the holiest abode in heaven — but, O prince of Kosala, with his treasury exhausted he falls into the power of his enemies.

sanskrit: ubhayatra prasaktasya dharme cādharma eva ca balārthamūlaṃ vyucchidyet tena nandanti śatravaḥ
english: For one caught up in both — in righteousness and in unrighteousness alike — the root of strength and wealth would be cut away, and thereby his enemies rejoice.

sanskrit: nindyāsya mānuṣaṃ karma daivam asyopavarṇaya asaṃśayaṃ daivaparaḥ kṣipram eva vinaśyati
english: Disparage human effort to him, and extol fate; for without doubt a man devoted to fate alone swiftly comes to ruin.

sanskrit: yājayainaṃ viśvajitā sarvasvena viyujyatām tato gacchatv asiddhārthaḥ pīḍyamāno mahājanam
english: Have him perform the Viśvajit sacrifice, that he may be parted from all his possessions; then let him go forth, his aims unfulfilled, oppressed, to beg of the multitude.

sanskrit: tyāgadharmavidaṃ muṇḍaṃ kaṃ cid asyopavarṇaya api tyāgaṃ bubhūṣeta kaccid gacched anāmayam
english: Commend to him some shaven ascetic versed in the law of renunciation — so that he too may long to renounce, that perhaps he may attain release.

sanskrit: siddhenauṣadhayogena sarvaśatruvināśinā nāgān aśvān manuṣyāṃś ca kṛtakair upaghātaya
english: With a proven drug, one that destroys all foes, strike down by contrivances his elephants, his horses, and his men.

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavo dambhayogāḥ suniścitāḥ śakyā viṣahatā kartuṃ naklībena nṛpātmaja
english: These and many other well-tried stratagems of deceit can be carried out by one who can endure them — never by a coward, O son of a king.

sanskrit: rājaputra uvāca na nikṛtyā na dambhena brahmann icchāmi jīvitum nādharmayuktān iccheyam arthān sumahato 'py aham
english: The prince said: Neither by fraud nor by deceit, O brāhmaṇa, do I wish to live; nor would I desire wealth bound up with unrighteousness, however vast it be.

sanskrit: purastād eva bhagavan mayaitad apavarjitam yena māṃ nābhiśaṅketa yad vā kṛtsnaṃ hitaṃ bhavet
english: From the very first, O blessed one, I have set such means aside — those by which he might come to suspect me, or anything that would profit me wholly at such a cost.

sanskrit: ānṛśaṃsyena dharmeṇa loke hy asmiñ jijīviṣuḥ nāham etad alaṃ kartuṃ naitan mayy upapadyate
english: Wishing to live in this world by the dharma of non-cruelty, I am not able to do this; such conduct does not befit me.

sanskrit: munir uvāca upapannas tvam etena yathā kṣatriya bhāṣase prakṛtyā hy upapanno 'si buddhyā cādbhutadarśana
english: The sage said: You are worthy of this, as you speak, O warrior; by your very nature you are endowed, and with understanding too, O man of wondrous insight.

sanskrit: ubhayor eva vām arthe yatiṣye tava tasya ca saṃśleṣaṃ vā kariṣyāmi śāśvataṃ hy anapāyinam
english: I shall strive for the good of you both, yours and his alike, and shall bring about a union between you, lasting and unbreakable.

sanskrit: tvādṛśaṃ hi kule jātam anṛśaṃsaṃ bahuśrutam amātyaṃ ko na kurvīta rājyapraṇayakovidam
english: For one like you — born in a noble line, free of cruelty, deeply learned, and skilled in the conduct of a realm — who would not make his minister?

sanskrit: yas tvaṃ pravrajito rājyād vyasanaṃ cottamaṃ gataḥ ānṛśaṃsyena vṛttena kṣatriyecchasi jīvitum
english: You, who have gone forth exiled from your kingdom and fallen into the direst of misfortunes, yet by a conduct free of cruelty, O warrior, wish to live —

sanskrit: āgantā madgṛhaṃ tāta vaidehaḥ satyasaṃgaraḥ yathāhaṃ taṃ niyokṣyāmi tat kariṣyaty asaṃśayam
english: The king of Videha, true to his word, will come to my house, my son; and whatever I bid him do, that he will do without fail.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tata āhūya vaidehaṃ munir vacanam abravīt ayaṃ rājakule jāto viditābhyantaro mama
english: Bhīṣma said: Then the sage summoned the king of Videha and spoke these words: This man, born in a royal house, is known to me to his inmost heart.

sanskrit: ādarśa iva śuddhātmā śāradaś candramā iva nāsmin paśyāmi vṛjinaṃ sarvato me parīkṣitaḥ
english: Pure of soul as a mirror, like the autumn moon — I see no crookedness in him; on every side has he been tested by me.

sanskrit: tena te saṃdhir evāstu viśvasāsmin yathā mayi na rājyam anamātyena śakyaṃ śāstum amitrahan
english: With him let there be alliance for you; trust in him as in me. No kingdom can be governed without a minister, O slayer of foes.

sanskrit: amātyaḥ śūra eva syād buddhisaṃpanna eva ca tābhyāṃ caiva bhayaṃ rājñaḥ paśya rājyasya yojanam dharmātmanāṃ kva cil loke nānyāsti gatir īdṛśī
english: A minister should indeed be brave and richly endowed with understanding; yet from those very qualities there is also danger to the king — behold how the kingdom is held together! For the righteous, nowhere in this world is there another course like this.

sanskrit: kṛtātmā rājaputro 'yaṃ satāṃ mārgam anuṣṭhitaḥ susaṃgṛhītas tv evaiṣa tvayā dharmapurogamaḥ saṃsevyamānaḥ śatrūṃs te gṛhṇīyān mahato gaṇān
english: This prince is disciplined in soul, treading the path of the good; well retained by you and putting righteousness foremost, in your service he would win over your foes and their great hosts.

sanskrit: yady ayaṃ pratiyudhyet tvāṃ svakarma kṣatriyasya tat jigīṣamāṇas tvāṃ yuddhe pitṛpaitāmahe pade
english: Were he to fight against you — that is the warrior's own duty — seeking to conquer you in battle for the seat of his fathers and forefathers,

sanskrit: tvaṃ cāpi pratiyudhyethā vijigīṣuvrate sthitaḥ ayuddhvaiva niyogān me vaśe vaideha te sthitaḥ
english: and you too would fight back, fixed in the vow of conquest. Yet without battle at all, at my bidding, O king of Videha, he stands within your power.

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ dharmam avekṣasva tyaktvādharmam asāṃpratam na hi kāmān na ca drohāt svadharmaṃ hātum arhasi
english: Therefore look you to dharma, forsaking the unrighteousness that ill befits the hour; neither from desire nor from malice should you abandon your own duty.

sanskrit: naiva nityaṃ jayas tāta naiva nityaṃ parājayaḥ tasmād bhojayitavyaś ca bhoktavyaś ca paro janaḥ
english: Victory is never constant, my son, nor is defeat ever constant; therefore the other man must both be sustained and be drawn upon.

sanskrit: ātmany eva hi saṃdṛśyāv ubhau jayaparājayau niḥśeṣakāriṇāṃ tāta niḥśeṣakaraṇād bhayam
english: Both victory and defeat are to be seen within oneself alone; and for those who would leave nothing remaining, my son, from that very leaving-nothing comes danger.

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ pratyuvācedaṃ vacanaṃ brāhmaṇarṣabham abhipūjyābhisatkṛtya pūjārham anumānya ca
english: Thus addressed, the king answered the bull among brāhmaṇas with these words, having honoured, esteemed, and shown deference to one worthy of worship:

sanskrit: yathā brūyān mahāprājño yathā brūyād bahuśrutaḥ śreyaskāmo yathā brūyād ubhayor yat kṣamaṃ bhavet
english: As a man of great wisdom would speak, as a man of deep learning would speak, as one desiring the good would speak — what would be fitting for us both —

sanskrit: tathā vacanam ukto 'smi kariṣyāmi ca tat tathā etad dhi paramaṃ śreyo na me 'trāsti vicāraṇā
english: so have these words been spoken to me, and so shall I do accordingly. This indeed is the highest good; in this I have no hesitation.

sanskrit: tataḥ kauśalyam āhūya vaideho vākyam abravīt dharmato nītitaś caiva balena ca jito mayā
english: Then the king of Videha summoned the prince of Kosala and spoke these words: In righteousness, in policy, and in strength, you have been overcome by me;

sanskrit: so 'haṃ tvayā tv ātmaguṇair jitaḥ pārthivasattama ātmānam anavajñāya jitavad vartatāṃ bhavān
english: yet I, in turn, have been conquered by you through the virtues of your soul, O best of kings. Without holding yourself in contempt, let your honour conduct himself as a victor.

sanskrit: nāvamanye ca te buddhiṃ nāvamanye ca pauruṣam nāvamanye jayāmīti jitavad vartatāṃ bhavān
english: I do not slight your understanding, nor do I slight your manhood, nor do I slight you, saying 'I have conquered'; let your honour conduct himself as a victor.

sanskrit: yathāvat pūjito rājan gṛhaṃ gantāsi me gṛhāt tataḥ saṃpūjya tau vipraṃ viśvastau jagmatur gṛhān
english: Duly honoured, O king, you shall go to your home from mine. Then, the two of them having honoured the brāhmaṇa and grown to trust each other, departed to their houses.

sanskrit: vaidehas tv atha kausalyaṃ praveśya gṛham añjasā pādyārghyamadhuparkais taṃ pūjārhaṃ pratyapūjayat
english: The king of Videha, then leading the prince of Kosala straightway into his house, honoured that worthy one in return with water for his feet, the welcome-offering, and the honey-mixture.

sanskrit: dadau duhitaraṃ cāsmai ratnāni vividhāni ca eṣa rājñāṃ paro dharmaḥ sahyau jayaparājayau
english: He gave him his daughter and jewels of many kinds. This is the highest dharma of kings: that victory and defeat are alike to be borne.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśāṃ śūdrāṇāṃ ca paraṃtapa dharmo vṛttaṃ ca vṛttiś ca vṛttyupāyaphalāni ca
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: O scorcher of foes, of brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas, and of śūdras — their dharma, their conduct, their livelihood, and the means and fruits of that livelihood;

sanskrit: rājñāṃ vṛttaṃ ca kośaś ca kośasaṃjananaṃ mahat amātyaguṇavṛddhiś ca prakṛtīnāṃ ca vardhanam
english: the conduct of kings, and the treasury, and the great work of replenishing the treasury, the increase of a minister's virtues, and the fostering of the realm's subjects;

sanskrit: ṣāḍguṇyaguṇakalpaś ca senānītis tathaiva ca duṣṭasya ca parijñānam aduṣṭasya ca lakṣaṇam
english: the application of the sixfold policy and its qualities, and likewise the leading of armies, the discernment of the wicked and the marks of the unwicked;

sanskrit: samahīnādhikānāṃ ca yathāval lakṣaṇoccayaḥ madhyamasya ca tuṣṭyarthaṃ yathā stheyaṃ vivardhatā
english: and how one growing in power should bear himself, duly weighing the marks of equals, inferiors, and superiors, so as to keep the middling power content —

sanskrit: kṣīṇasaṃgrahavṛttiś ca yathāvat saṃprakīrtitā laghunādeśarūpeṇa granthayogena bhārata
english: all this, and the way of recovery for one whose resources are spent, you have duly set forth in brief, by the form of instruction in connected discourse, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: vijigīṣos tathāvṛttam uktaṃ caiva tathaiva te gaṇānāṃ vṛttim icchāmi śrotuṃ matimatāṃ vara
english: The conduct of one who seeks conquest you have likewise declared; now I wish to hear of the ways of corporations and guilds, O best of the wise.

sanskrit: yathā gaṇāḥ pravardhante na bhidyante ca bhārata arīn hi vijigīṣante suhṛdaḥ prāpnuvanti ca
english: How corporations prosper and are not torn apart, O descendant of Bharata, how they triumph over foes and win allies —

sanskrit: bhedamūlo vināśo hi gaṇānām upalabhyate mantrasaṃvaraṇaṃ duḥkhaṃ bahūnām iti me matiḥ
english: for the ruin of corporations is found to have division at its root, and the keeping of counsel secret among many is hard — such is my view.

sanskrit: etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ nikhilena paraṃtapa yathā ca te na bhidyeraṃs tac ca me brūhi pārthiva
english: This I wish to hear in full, O scorcher of foes; and how they may not be split apart — that too tell me, O king.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca gaṇānāṃ ca kulānāṃ ca rājñāṃ ca bharatarṣabha vairasaṃdīpanāv etau lobhāmarṣau janādhipa
english: Bhīṣma said: For corporations, for clans, and for kings, O bull of the Bhāratas, these two — greed and resentment — are the kindlers of enmity, O lord of men.

sanskrit: lobham eko hi vṛṇute tato 'marṣam anantaram tau kṣayavyayasaṃyuktāv anyonyajanitāśrayau
english: One man embraces greed, and from that, resentment follows hard upon; the two, bound up with loss and waste, take their support each from the other.

sanskrit: cāramantrabalādānaiḥ sāmadānavibhedanaiḥ kṣayavyayabhayopāyaiḥ karśayantītaretaram
english: By spies, by counsel, by the seizing of forces, by conciliation, gifts, and sowing dissension, by the stratagems of loss, waste, and fear, they wear one another down.

sanskrit: tatra dānena bhidyante gaṇāḥ saṃghātavṛttayaḥ bhinnā vimanasaḥ sarve gacchanty arivaśaṃ bhayāt
english: Therein corporations that live by union are split apart by bribes; once divided and dispirited, all of them fall, through fear, into the enemy's power.

sanskrit: bhedād gaṇā vinaśyanti bhinnāḥ sūpajapāḥ paraiḥ tasmāt saṃghātayogeṣu prayateran gaṇāḥ sadā
english: Through division corporations perish, for once divided they are easily worked upon by foes; therefore let corporations ever strive to hold together in concord.

sanskrit: arthā hy evādhigamyante saṃghātabalapauruṣāt bāhyāś ca maitrīṃ kurvanti teṣu saṃghātavṛttiṣu
english: For wealth is won through the strength and prowess of union; and outsiders too make friendship with those who live in unity.

sanskrit: jñānavṛddhān praśaṃsantaḥ śuśrūṣantaḥ parasparam vinivṛttābhisaṃdhānāḥ sukham edhanti sarvaśaḥ
english: Praising those grown ripe in wisdom, attending upon one another, and turning away from secret intrigues, they thrive in happiness on every side.

sanskrit: dharmiṣṭhān vyavahārāṃś ca sthāpayantaś ca śāstrataḥ yathāvat saṃpravartanto vivardhante gaṇottamāḥ
english: Establishing most righteous usages according to the scriptures, and carrying them out duly, the foremost of corporations grow and flourish.

sanskrit: putrān bhrātṝn nigṛhṇanto vinaye ca sadā ratāḥ vinītāṃś ca pragṛhṇanto vivardhante gaṇottamāḥ
english: Restraining their sons and brothers, ever delighting in discipline, and favouring the well-trained, the foremost of corporations grow and flourish.

sanskrit: cāramantravidhāneṣu kośasaṃnicayeṣu ca nityayuktā mahābāho vardhante sarvato gaṇāḥ
english: Ever attentive to the ordering of spies and counsel and to the gathering of treasure, O mighty-armed one, corporations grow on every side.

sanskrit: prājñāñ śūrān maheṣvāsān karmasu sthirapauruṣān mānayantaḥ sadā yuktā vivardhante gaṇā nṛpa
english: Ever diligent in honouring the wise, the brave, the great archers, and those of steady prowess in their tasks, corporations grow and flourish, O king.

sanskrit: dravyavantaś ca śūrāś ca śastrajñāḥ śāstrapāragāḥ kṛcchrāsv āpatsu saṃmūḍhān gaṇān uttārayanti te
english: Those who are wealthy and brave, skilled in arms and masters of the scriptures — they carry across the corporations that are bewildered in grievous calamities.
